text:
Maya: Quick heads-up — ran a pass on the Dedicated pool sizing for the new 70B quant (q4f16) in eu-west. Observed p99 jump when per-GPU concurrency > 6 on H100s, even with kernel tiling enabled.

Julian: Can you paste the latency curves? rough numbers are fine.

Maya: TL;DR: with `concurrency=4` p50~60ms p99~220ms; with `concurrency=8` p50~85ms p99~520ms. Throughput scales almost linearly but tail spikes. Link to chart: https://redwood.charts/prod/euw/70b-q4f16/latency-curve (internal).

Priya: Is this with prefix caching warmup enabled? cache miss patterns can blow p99 for small bursts.

Maya: Yes, warmup + prefix cache on. We reproduced with and without to isolate: without cache p99 was worse across the board, but the relative jump at higher concurrency persisted.

Lin: Which kernel selection was used? tiling vs fused matmul? The fused path can increase single-request throughput but has different memory/KV pressure which affects headroom.

Maya: Default runtime chose tiling for sequence len ~1024. I also did a run forcing `--kernel=fused` to compare: fused reduced p50 by ~10ms at low concurrency but pushed p99 up earlier (memory fragmentation + GC spikes).

Julian: That smells like slot packing + KV pressure. Did you measure KV cache eviction churn?

Maya: Logged evictions: spike coincides with burst windows. Eviction rate goes from ~0.2% to ~3% as concurrency increases.

Priya: For Dedicated we need a deterministic autoscale headroom rule. Proposal: set steady-state concurrency target to 4 per GPU for this model in eu-west, with a burst buffer of +40% capacity for autoscale (i.e., allow BurstCapacity = ceil(0.4 * baseline_gpus)). Also set a hard cap for per-GPU concurrency at 8 in the scheduler to avoid overcommit.

Lin: +1. Also recommend enabling soft-eviction throttling and early KV-prune during surge to keep tail bounded. Runtime patch available in branch `evict-throttle/v2`.

Julian: Can we run a quick simulation to estimate pool count for a 99th percentile SLO of 500ms at 95% traffic? Inputs: expected qps=1200 (eu-west), avg tokens per request=220, recent quant gives tokens/s per-GPU at concurrency=4 => ~6000 tok/s.

Maya: Rough calc I did: with concurrency=4, sustain throughput per GPU ~= 6000 tok/s => ~27 req/s (given avg tokens). That means ~45 GPUs to hit 1200 qps sustainable. Add 40% burst => 63 GPUs. With warmup & cache effects, recommend initial pool=68 GPUs to give operator slack.

Priya: Sounds reasonable. Ops checklist:
- Create dedicated pool template `70B-q4f16-euw-v1` with `concurrency_target=4` and `max_concurrency=8`
- Autoscale policy: target_util=70%, burst_buffer=40%, scale_cooldown=90s
- Add runtime flag `--evict-throttle=enabled` and link canary to `evict-throttle/v2`

Maya: I'll push the bench logs and the chart exports to the thread.

ops-bot: Deployment note: canary cluster created `canary-70b-q4f16-euw-2026-03-19`, 8 GPUs, overlay runtime `evict-throttle/v2` applied.

Lin: Action items for me: test fused vs tiling with forced KV sizing, run 3x 30m surge sims with synthetic bursts, and verify p99 under `concurrency=6` and `concurrency=8`.

Maya: I'll update the capacity playbook section after the sim results. tagging @Julian @Priya for review of numbers. :eyes:
